nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, and let $p$ be the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$. Then $s$ is $p$ followed by the list obtained by dropping the first $|p|$ elements of $s$, where $|p|$ is the length of $p$.
nodes.title: A list is its common prefix with another list followed by the rest

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality. If the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is $t$, then $s$ is $t$ followed by the list obtained by dropping the first $|t|$ elements of $s$, where $|t|$ is the length of $t$.
nodes.title: When the common prefix is the second list, the first list extends it

nodes.summary: The trie built from the empty list is the empty trie, and the trie built from a list with head $(k, v)$ and tail $L$ is the trie built from $L$ with the value $v$ inserted at the key $k$. Later pairs in the list are thus inserted first, so on duplicate keys the head-most value wins.
nodes.title: Radix trie built from a list of key-value pairs

nodes.summary: Write $uv$ for the list $u$ followed by the list $v$. For lists $p$, $s$ and $t$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $ps$ and $pt$ is $p$ followed by the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: A shared prefix factors out of the longest common prefix

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, let $p$ be their longest common prefix, of length $n$, and let $s'$ and $t'$ be the lists obtained from $s$ and $t$ by dropping their first $n$ elements. Then $s$ is $p$ followed by $s'$, $t$ is $p$ followed by $t'$, and either $s'$ is empty, or $t'$ is empty, or $s'$ and $t'$ are both nonempty with different first elements.
nodes.title: Longest common prefix in terms of dropped remainders

nodes.summary: Let $s$, $t$ and $u$ be lists over a type with decidable equality. If $s$ is $t$ followed by $u$, then the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is $t$.
nodes.title: The longest common prefix of a list and its prefix

nodes.summary: For every list $s$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $s$ and $s$ is $s$.
nodes.title: Longest common prefix of a list with itself

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type with decidable equality, with longest common prefix $p$. Then there are lists $s'$ and $t'$ such that $s$ is $p$ followed by $s'$, $t$ is $p$ followed by $t'$, and either $s'$ is empty, or $t'$ is empty, or $s'$ and $t'$ are both nonempty with different first elements.
nodes.title: Characterization of the longest common prefix

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with decidable equality, the longest common prefix of $s$ and $t$ is defined by recursion: it is empty if $s$ or $t$ is empty; if $s$ has first element $a$ and rest $s'$, and $t$ has first element $b$ and rest $t'$, it is $a$ followed by the longest common prefix of $s'$ and $t'$ when $a = b$, and empty when $a \ne b$.
nodes.title: Longest common prefix

nodes.summary: For all types $\alpha$ and $\beta$, the empty radix trie whose keys are lists over $\alpha$ and whose values lie in $\beta$ is valid.
nodes.title: The empty radix trie is valid

nodes.summary: The empty radix trie is the single node that stores no value and has no child edges; it contains no key-value entries.
nodes.title: Empty radix trie

nodes.summary: The entries of a radix trie are its key-value pairs, listed recursively. For a node with child edges $(\ell_1, t_1), \dots, (\ell_n, t_n)$ in stored order, the list starts with the pair $(\varepsilon, v)$, where $\varepsilon$ is the empty key, if the node stores a value $v$; it continues with the entries of $t_1$ with $\ell_1$ prepended to every key, then the entries of $t_2$ with $\ell_2$ prepended, and so on up…
nodes.title: Entries of a radix trie

nodes.summary: Given a symbol $c$ and a list of edges, each a pair of a label (a list of symbols) and a subtree, this returns the first edge in the list whose label starts with $c$, or nothing if no label starts with $c$.
nodes.title: Edge search by first symbol

nodes.summary: For a valid radix trie $t$ and a list $p$ of symbols, prefix search for $p$ in $t$ succeeds if and only if some stored key $k$ of $t$ has $p$ as a prefix.
nodes.title: Prefix search is correct on valid radix tries

nodes.summary: For a radix trie $t$ and a pattern $p$ (a list of symbols), prefix search returns a boolean computed as follows. If $p$ is empty, it is true exactly when $t$ stores at least one key. Otherwise let $c$ be the first symbol of $p$ and take the first child edge of the root whose label starts with $c$; if there is none, the answer is false. If that edge has label $\ell$ and subtree $s$, then: when $p$ is a prefix of…
nodes.title: Prefix search in a radix trie

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid radix trie, then for every key $k$ and value $v$, the trie obtained by inserting $v$ at $k$ in $t$ is valid.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves validity of radix tries

nodes.summary: Inserting a value $v$ at a key $k$ (a list of symbols) into a radix trie works as follows. If $k$ is empty, the root's value becomes $v$. Otherwise let $c$ be the first symbol of $k$. If no child edge of the root has a label starting with $c$, a new edge labelled $k$ leading to a leaf storing $v$ is added after the existing edges. Otherwise take the first such edge, with label $\ell$ and subtree $s$, let $q$ be the…
nodes.title: Insertion into a radix trie

nodes.summary: If $t$ is a valid radix trie, then its list of stored keys has no duplicates.
nodes.title: Stored keys of a valid radix trie are distinct

nodes.summary: The stored keys of a radix trie form the list of the keys of its entries, in the same order.
nodes.title: Stored keys of a radix trie

nodes.summary: For a list $L$ of key-value pairs, if $(k, v)$ belongs to $L$, then looking up $k$ in the radix trie built from $L$ returns some value.
nodes.title: Every listed key is present in the built radix trie

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of key-value pairs, whose keys are lists over $\gamma$, in which no key occurs twice. If the pair $(k, v)$ occurs in $L$, then looking up $k$ in the radix trie built from $L$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup in a radix trie built from a list with distinct keys

nodes.summary: For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty radix trie returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty radix trie

nodes.summary: For a valid radix trie $T$, every key $k$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if the pair $(k, v)$ occurs in the list of entries of $T$.
nodes.title: Lookup agrees with the entries of a valid radix trie

nodes.summary: For every radix trie $T$, all keys $k \ne k'$ and every value $v$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $T$ by inserting $v$ at $k'$ gives the same result as looking up $k$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a radix trie leaves lookups of other keys unchanged

nodes.summary: For every radix trie $T$, key $k$ and value $v$, looking up $k$ in the trie obtained from $T$ by inserting $v$ at $k$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup of a key just inserted into a radix trie

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a nonempty key with first symbol $c$, and consider a node with children $C$ (a list of edges, each a label with a subtree), whatever value the node stores. If no edge of $C$ has a label starting with $c$, looking up $k$ at the node returns no value. Otherwise let $(\ell, T')$ be the first such edge of $C$: if the longest common prefix of $k$ and $\ell$ is $\ell$, the lookup returns the lookup in $T'$ of…
nodes.title: Radix trie lookup of a nonempty key at a node

nodes.summary: Looking up a key, a list over $\alpha$, in a radix trie returns an optional value. At a node, the empty key returns the value stored at the node, if any. A nonempty key $k$ with first symbol $c$ goes to the first child edge whose label starts with $c$. If there is no such edge, or its label $\ell$ is not a prefix of $k$, the lookup returns no value; otherwise it continues in the subtree of that edge with $k$ minus…
nodes.title: Radix trie lookup

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of key-value pairs and every key $k$, $k$ is a stored key of the radix trie built from $L$ if and only if the pair $(k, v)$ occurs in $L$ for some value $v$.
nodes.title: Keys of a radix trie built from a list

nodes.summary: For a valid radix trie $T$ and every key $k$, $k$ is a stored key of $T$ if and only if looking up $k$ in $T$ returns some value.
nodes.title: Stored keys of a valid radix trie are the keys with a successful lookup

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of key-value pairs, if looking up a key $k$ in the radix trie built from $L$ returns a value $v$, then the pair $(k, v)$ occurs in $L$.
nodes.title: Lookups in a radix trie built from a list come from the list

nodes.summary: If a radix-trie node with child edges $(\ell_1, t_1), \dots, (\ell_n, t_n)$ is valid, then the first symbols of the labels $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_n$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Sibling edge labels start with distinct symbols

nodes.summary: For types $\alpha$ and $\beta$, a radix trie with keys that are lists over $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is a node made of an optional value in $\beta$ and a finite list of child edges, each a pair of a label, which is a list over $\alpha$, and a radix trie (the subtree at the end of the edge).
nodes.title: Radix trie

nodes.summary: Given a symbol $c$, an edge $e$ (a pair of a label and a radix trie) and a list of child edges, this operation replaces the first edge of the list whose label starts with $c$ by $e$ and keeps all other edges in order. If no label in the list starts with $c$, it appends $e$ at the end of the list.
nodes.title: Replacing the child edge for a symbol

nodes.summary: If a radix-trie node is valid, then for each of its child edges, the subtree at the end of that edge is path-compressed at its root: its root stores a value or has at least two child edges.
nodes.title: Children of a valid node are path-compressed

nodes.summary: A radix trie is path-compressed at its root when its root node stores a value or has at least two child edges.
nodes.title: Path-compressed root

nodes.summary: Validity of radix tries is defined inductively: a node is valid when every label of its child edges is nonempty, the first symbols of the labels of its child edges are pairwise distinct, and for each child edge the subtree at its end is valid and path-compressed at its root (its root stores a value or has at least two child edges).
nodes.title: Valid radix trie

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
